description: SWIFT message type for single customer credit transfers. Carries originator/beneficiary information required by TFR Travel Rule. Fields: F20 (reference), F23B (bank operation code), F50 (ordering customer — name/address), F59 (beneficiary customer — name/address/account). Used for international wire transfers.

SWIFT message for bank-to-bank transfers. Does NOT carry originator/beneficiary customer information. Used for funding covers and interbank settlements. AML risk: MT202 can be misused to hide originator in cover payment structures.

SWIFT message for cover payment transfers, introduced to address AML concern with standard MT202. MT202 COV carries full originator/beneficiary information in field 50a/59a. Mandatory when MT202 is used as cover for an MT103 customer payment. Introduced 2009 per SWIFT guidance.

SWIFT free-format message used for various purposes in the customer payments category. Used for inquiries, investigations, and exceptions. AML relevance: MT199 requests can be used to query missing payment information under TFR.

ISO 20022 equivalent of MT103 for customer credit transfers. Richer data structure: structured address, LEI, IBAN, purpose codes, remittance information. Mandatory fields for TFR compliance: FIToFICstmrCdtTrf/DbtrAgt, Dbtr, Cdtr, CdtrAgt. Mandatory for SWIFT cross-border payments from Nov 2025.
ISO 20022 equivalent of MT202 and MT202COV for bank-to-bank transfers. Includes cover payment sub-type (pacs.009 COV) with originator/beneficiary information. Mandatory for SWIFT from November 2025.

ISO 20022 message providing end-of-day account statement to account holder. Contains detailed transaction information including originator/beneficiary. Used for reconciliation and AML transaction monitoring data feeds.

canonical_name: SWIFT — Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication
description: Global provider of secure financial messaging services. Based in Belgium. Over 11,000 institutions in 200+ countries. Messages processed: 40+ million daily. SWIFT exclusion is a key sanctions enforcement tool. SWIFT operates gpi (global payments innovation) for faster cross-border payments.

Unique 8-11 character identifier for financial institutions in SWIFT messages. Format: BANKCCLL[BBB] where BANK=institution code, CC=country, LL=location, BBB=branch. Required in all SWIFT messages. Also known as SWIFT code.

canonical_name: LEI in ISO 20022 Payments (Legal Entity Identifier)
description: ISO 20022 payment messages (pacs.008/009) include structured fields for LEI (Legal Entity Identifier) of ordering and beneficiary parties. LEI in payments enables automated sanctions screening and AML analysis. SWIFT gpi requires LEI for institutional counterparties.

SWIFT's enhanced cross-border payment service. Mandatory for SWIFT member banks from 2019. Requirements: track and trace capability (UETR unique end-to-end transaction reference), same-day processing, fee transparency. AML: gpi enables end-to-end payment tracking, improving originator/beneficiary tracing.

A unique 36-character UUID assigned to each SWIFT payment transaction. Mandatory for gpi payments. Enables full end-to-end tracking of payment from originator to beneficiary. Critical for sanctions screening, AML investigations, and correspondent banking transparency.

International standard for financial industry electronic messaging. Richer data content than legacy SWIFT MT messages: structured addresses, legal entity identifiers, purpose codes. SWIFT mandatory migration: cross-border payments to ISO 20022 from November 2022 (full migration by November 2025).

Payment where a bank sends customer instructions directly to the beneficiary bank (MT103 serial) while simultaneously using MT202 for the interbank settlement (cover). MT202 COV introduced to ensure originator/beneficiary info is carried in the cover leg. Historical AML concern: early MT202 use enabled originator info stripping.

Field 50a, 50F, or 50K in MT103 message containing the ordering customer (originator) information. Required for TFR Travel Rule compliance. 50F: structured name/address format (preferred for AML). 50K: unstructured format (being phased out). Must contain: name, account, address.

Field 59 or 59F in MT103 message containing the beneficiary (payee) information. Required for TFR Travel Rule compliance. 59F: structured format with account, name, address. Must contain: name, account, address. Checked against sanctions lists by beneficiary bank.

Banks must screen SWIFT payments against sanctions lists before processing. Screening occurs at: originating bank (pre-send), correspondent banks (at receipt), and beneficiary bank (at receipt). Filter hits require investigation and may require freezing funds and reporting.

TFR Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 requires originator/beneficiary information with payments — operationally implemented via SWIFT MT103 fields 50/59 or ISO 20022 pacs.008 debtor/creditor fields. MT202COV and pacs.009COV carry this for cover payments. TFR compliance relies on correct SWIFT field population.

Exclusion from SWIFT is a major sanctions tool. Russia: major banks excluded from SWIFT from March 2022. Iran: excluded 2012, partially restored 2016, excluded again 2018. DPRK: excluded. Disconnection forces use of alternative messaging channels (often less transparent).
